newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-DEVERS PULLS OUT OF U.S. CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-DEVERS PULLS OUT OF U.S. CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Double Olympic women's 100-meter champion Gail Devers pulled out of the U.S. athletics championships Friday in an apparent dispute over possible wild card entries to the world championships.
A meet spokesman said Devers, who had clocked 10.99 seconds in a preliminary race on Thursday, had officially withdrawn because of "a sore right calf muscle."
But three hours before the race, Bob Kersee, Devers's coach, told Reuters he was considering withdrawing Devers and heptathlon world record-holder Jackie Joyner-Kersee from the championships.

Kersee expressed displeasure over talk of giving world championship wild card entries to double Olympic and world champion Michael Johnson and three-time decathlon world champion Dan O'Brien, who are both sidelined by injury and unable to compete in this qualifying event.
"Why should I risk injury to my athletes here if they are going to grant wild cards," Kersee said.
He later said Joyner-Kersee would compete in the championships in the women's long jump beginning Saturday.

Currently only the top three finishers at U.S. national championships are eligible for the U.S. world championship team. But U.S. track officials said they would welcome the IAAF granting wild card entries to the Athens world championships for 1995 world champions.

IAAF spokesman Giorgio Reineri said Friday: "If the U.S. federation says it would support such a move, this in certain measure opens the way for the IAAF to examine the possibility of inviting champions and world record holders to Athens."

That would offer Devers, the world 100-meter hurdles champion, and world record-holder Joyner-Kersee an opportunity to compete in Athens, along with Johnson, O'Brien and injured world women's 100-meter champion Gwen Torrence.
